_meta.indication: Effient is a P2Y12 platelet inhibitor indicated for the reduction of thrombotic cardiovascular events (including stent thrombosis) in patients with acute coronary syndrome who are to be managed with PCI (patients with UA/NSTEMI, and patients with STEMI when managed with primary or delayed PCI).

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in reviewed documents for TRITON-TIMI 38 (null)
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, international, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group study comparing Effient to clopidogrel, each added to aspirin and standard therapy (prasugrel 60 mg loading dose then 10 mg once daily vs clopidogrel 300 mg loading dose then 75 mg once daily).
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with acute coronary syndrome (UA/NSTEMI presenting within 72 hours of symptom onset, or STEMI) who were to be managed with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary efficacy endpoint: composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal MI, or nonfatal stroke in the UA/NSTEMI population (with hierarchical analysis in the overall ACS and STEMI populations).
pivotal_trials.n: 13,608 patients in the intent-to-treat population (6,813 prasugrel; 6,795 clopidogrel).
pivotal_trials.result: In UA/NSTEMI, primary endpoint 9.3% (Effient) vs 11.2% (clopidogrel), HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.73, 0.93), p=0.002. Overall ACS: 9.4% vs 11.5%, HR 0.81 (95% CI 0.73, 0.90), p<0.001. Treatment effect driven predominantly by reduction in nonfatal MI.

key_safety: Bleeding, including life-threatening and fatal bleeding, is the most common adverse reaction. In TRITON-TIMI 38 non-CABG-related TIMI Major bleeding occurred in 2.2% (Effient) vs 1.7% (clopidogrel), HR 1.32; TIMI life-threatening 1.3% vs 0.8%; fatal bleeding 0.3% vs 0.1%. Among 437 patients undergoing CABG, CABG-related TIMI Major/Minor bleeding was 14.1% vs 4.5%. Bleeding led to drug discontinuation in 2.5% vs 1.4%.
target_moa: Prasugrel is a thienopyridine prodrug that is rapidly metabolized to a pharmacologically active metabolite which irreversibly binds the platelet P2Y12 ADP receptor, inhibiting ADP-mediated platelet activation and aggregation.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: BLEEDING RISK — Effient can cause significant, sometimes fatal, bleeding. Do not use in patients with active pathological bleeding or a history of TIA or stroke. In patients >=75 years Effient is generally not recommended due to increased risk of fatal and intracranial bleeding and uncertain benefit, except in high-risk patients.

rems.type: A REMS consisting of a Medication Guide, a communication plan, an implementation system, and a timetable for submission of assessments was approved.

advisory_committee.vote: A public presentation to the Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Advisory Committee was planned for February 3, 2009 to discuss the neoplasm imbalance, salt-to-base form conversion/PPI bioinequivalence, and bleeding risk. The reviewed documents state only that the meeting was planned; they do not confirm that it was held or report any vote tally.

summary.text: Effient (prasugrel) was submitted as a 505(b)(1) NDA on 26 December 2007 and reviewed under Priority status. Approval was based on the single large, randomized, double-blind TRITON-TIMI 38 trial. A Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Advisory Committee meeting was convened (planned February 3, 2009) to discuss neoplasm imbalance, salt-to-base form conversion/PPI bioinequivalence, and bleeding risk. The drug carries a boxed warning for bleeding risk and was approved with a REMS and post-marketing requirements/commitments.

requirement.text: An open-label trial of ex vivo reversal of platelet inhibition by exogenous platelets as a function of time and plasma level of prasugrel active metabolite in 28 normal volunteers administered a single 60-mg loading dose of prasugrel plus aspirin 325 mg.

citations.quote: - An open-label trial of *ex vivo* reversal of platelet inhibition by exogenous platelets as a function of time and plasma level of prasugrel active metabolite in 28 normal volunteers administered a single 60-mg loading dose of prasugrel plus aspirin 325 mg. The methods should be similar to those described by Vilahur *et al.*, 2007. J. Thromb Haemost 5:82. Descriptive statistics should be reported.
